crit: The datasets are chosen based on the class imbalance ratio; the imbalance ratio of the selected datasets ranges from 1.38 to 41.4; the selected datasets are considered as benchmark and widely used in the literature as summarized by [29].
notes: Table 1 (pdf p.8, printed 118646) prints only #features, #classes and IR (no #instances, no minority counts). Binarised sets (Yeast1, Vehicle1, Glass6, Yeast3-6) carry KEEL two-class file names and KEEL is named as a source; the paper never says the authors binarised anything, hence binarised_by=repository (inferred from names + stated source). Four multi-class sets kept native (Penbased 10, Contraceptive 3, Dermatology 6, Thyroid 3 classes). minority_rule: the method's own mean-size threshold (mu = |D|/#classes) defines minority vs majority for all datasets; for the KEEL two-class sets the split is otherwise repository-defined. [29] is a review (Spelmen & Porkodi 2018) cited only for the popularity claim, not as the source of the list, so benchmark_inherited_from not stated. Inclusion of multi-class data matches the method's stated scope (binary and multi-class) but no explicit selection reason is given for that, so method-target not coded. Table 3 first row is printed 'River' (Table 1 says 'Liver'). CBHSID cells printed with a space before the ± sign (e.g. '0.9656 ±0.012'). Tables 1 and 3 are images in the text layer; values read from the rendered PDF pages 8-9.
